SEPTEMBER, 1989      Page  Reply

      HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
      ----------------------
Letters are accepted in any form
for publication in OUTLETTERS:
BASIC PRINT or DATA; handwritten
or typed copy; all wordprocessor
files (please state which!) or a
simple JOTTER program is in our
Issue 2(Disk #4).The easiest for
us to edit are Tasword 2 files
with the right margin set at 32.

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Chris Clayton, CARLISLE

Dear Ron & Brian,
   I was very pleased to see the
new minichars screen font for
Wordmaster (OUTLET 23). However,
when I loaded it in it worked,
but much of Wordmaster didn't!
eg. the printer is disabled, and
various Wordmaster extension
programs,including the Typeliner
Pagemaker,are corrupted.Any idea
on what is causing this?I wasn't
able to follow your instruction
to CLEAR as this produces the
message 'Ramtop no good'.Perhaps
the problem is associated with
the fact that my machine's 128K?
   Also, I couldn't get OUTPRINT
to work on OUTLET 23 files!
     Best wishes - Chris Clayton

To Chris Clayton from Brian


Sorry! I put CLEAR 5E3(5000)when
I meant CLEAR 5E4 (50000)! I've
re-tried the font and it seems
O.K. in WORDMASTER so try again
and let me know...


I tested OUTPRINT with #23 files
and the only problem is with big
files. I've now heard from Mike
Haine (see next OUTLETTER) that
OUTPRINT can't handle files
larger than 40 pages.Sorry again
but you might try his partial
mod (I've not yet)until his full
mod arrives.

                  - Brian

From:      Mike Haine.
           "Riverside"
           Welsh Road
            Offchurch
         Leamington Spa
            CV33 9AQ

        Tel: 0926 315884
        Prestel 788832249

Dear Eds,

I have a few comments to make on
various letters, mainly concern-
ing printers.

Re:Gordon Henderson:What printer
and interface do you use? As
Brian has said before,it is hard
to help sort out problems unless
full info is given on set ups
and the effect.

Re: Frank Harris and his crash-
ing problem:- I have an ammeter
in my 9V supply lead. With
Interface 1, VTX 5000 & Kempston
E the current is hardly any
greater than with no add-ons. On
the other hand when the
microdrive is run the current
increases by up to 30%. Thus if
there is a problem with current
pulling the voltage down, then
it should occur when the drives
are switched on. I should be
surprised if the problem is not
a bad contact on the 9V plug.

Since I soldered a lead straight
onto the board such problems as
this have practically disappear-
ed.

Re:Alan knight etc: Can you give
more detail of the OK1 Microline
192.? Does it have a DOT
ADDRESSABLE GRAPHICS (DAG) mode?
How many pins? Have you a list
of control codes?

Gordon Henderson:- The routines
used in OUTPRINT will COPY
anything which can be put on the
screen and in any of at least 4
sizes, provided the printer used
has a DAG facility.

Allister McColl:- The paper size
problem can be easily dealt with
by changing the'skip' value. You
will find this at 64955 (check
PRINT PEEK 64955 should print
the value '9' on the screen. If
so,POKE 64955,15 should be about
right for your longer paper.

Trevor Wright:- Could you write
me with details of your set up
and example of effect. With my
set up, Spectrum+, Epson RX 80
with Kempston intfc.E everything
prints perfectly, provided the
original text format is ok.and
is less than about 42 pages
long. If longer the prog locks
up. This can be partially
overcome by adding the following
line to the BASIC prog:-

350 IF PEEK 34818 > 40 THEN POKE
34818,40

This line prevents the pages
greater than 40 being decoded,
viewed, or printed. This is
better than before and I shall
send in a mod to print the whole
lot shortly.

A small point: Instead of 'F' &
'B' to go to next & previous
pages I use the arrow keys since
they are availabe on the bottom
line on the +keyboard.The change
is made in OUTPRINT Basic line
520 by putting CHR$ 9 & CHR$ 8
instead of "F" & B". (Brian why
not have "F" OR CHR$ 9....?) The
following microprog should help
you sort your printer problems
concerning DAG. Having initiated
the i'face(TOKENS MUST BE OFF!!)

  5 INPUT "DAG CODE? (76,89 OR
90. )"; C ;  "BYTES  (<256)";I;"
& J (keep small)";J
 10 LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ C;CHR$
I;CHR$ J;
 20 INPUT "X (<256) ";X:FOR N=1
TO I+256*J:LPRINT CHR$ X;:NEXT N

"27" then c sent to the printer
should put it in DAG mode(single
double or quadruple density
depending whether c is 76, 89,
or 90); I + 256 * J tells it the
number of bytes to be sent in
that mode and it will not come
out of it until that number has
been sent.

The value of X determines which
printer pins are fired. If X=1
only the bottom pin fires, if 2
the next up 4,the next and 7,
the bottom 3(What!Forgotten your
Binary's? - See the article on
numbers in OUTLET No.6 ). If you
put I=8 & X=1 then 8 bytes will
be printed like an underline.
With X=255 a solid block one
char long is printed....

If not you have not got into DAG
mode, so check the CODES with
your instruction book. In
OUTPRINT these Codes are sent
before each print operation.They
are in a string of codes from
64953 and include...

   27,78,9,27,51,24,27,c,144,3

The first 3 set the skip to 9
lines; the next 3 set the line
spacing to 24/216" (This gives
contiguous graphics); and the
last are for DAG mode with 144 +
256 * 3 = 912 bytes which is for
the 3 column line with spaces...

If your set up is giving the DAG
mode OK but still gives problems
check the SKIP & line spacing
codes.

If you still have problems do
not hesitate to write to me.
Anything sorted out will be
contributed to OUTLET. Doing it
all thro'these pages can be very
slow (ie a month delay at least
and can be 2). My address etc.
is at the start of this letter.

           Mike Haine.


Thanks Mike.Re:keys,I could name
six pairs that are popular but
it's really personal choice and
we can't satisfy everyone.

As Mike says,please write direct
to him on these printer problems
if you wish, for faster response
time and more direct help.

From Ron Smith, WATFORD

Dear Ron & Brian,

Thanks for the LEAGUE COMPILER
program correction in OUTLET 23
- no fault now with the GO SUB.

One thing puzzles me though. You
said you could not get the fault
- how come when a GO TO instead
of GOSUB was there to create the
fault?

I have 8 OUTLET discs (+D) now
and am gradually catching up
with past issues. The only moan
I have is that the +D never
seems to have any programs of
interest for it or about it.Only
the Opus seems to be favoured.

Instructions to "ERASE ALL" by
pressing E in some programs do
not work with the +D. I'm sure
many more owners of the +D set
up,and there are plenty of them,
would purchase OUTLET if they
knew that programs for the +D
were a regular feature.It's like
the weekly Popular Computing
Weekly. Try and find a mention
of the SPECTRUM! The conclusion
I have come to is that all the
debates of which is the best
computer - the Amiga or Atari ST
- it must be the SPECTRUM as
nobody writes to knock it!

All the best.
              Regards,

              Ron Smith

To Ron Smith from Brian

Good question! I don't know why
I couldn't get LEAGUE COMPILER
to crash! I can only guess that,
as with all programs, ONE person
testing, no matter how hard he
tries to vary his testing, may
always do things a certain way -
in a certain style. Another
person comes along and uses a
different route through the
program or uses different keys
and immediately crashes it!

As for system-specific programs,
we are dependant to a great
extent on what is contributed. I
don't have a +D so I can't write
anything.Ron(who has a Disciple)
is too busy dealing with orders!

However, in this VERY issue we
have DISC FILER for the +D and
Disciple only! I have written to
MGT but have not received any
support whatsoever from them.
Anyone else like to hassle them?

PCW give very poor coverage of
the Spectrum considering its
huge user-base. I can only guess
their questionnaires in previous
years showed they had a very low
readership of Spectrum users?

It is important the routine to
"ERASE ALL BUT" works properly.
Can you describe EXACTLY what
result you DO get? E.g. RESET or
NO response to the keypress or
an error message (if so what?).
Thanks.Anyone else with a +D had
this problem?          - Brian

         Steven Watkins,
   101 St.Nicolas Park Drive,
     Nuneaton, Warwickshire,
            CV11 6DZ.


Dear Ron/Brian,

My setup comprises of a +2,Kemp-
ston mouse, +D, Twoface, Micro-
vitec 653 colour monitor and a
Serial 8056 printer. This setup
suits my every need as a student
except for the printer.

At the moment I am saving for a
Star LC10, but it will take a
while and in the meantime I need
to print graphics on my 8056. I
have tried a variety of programs
but to no avail.They just crash.

On the subject of Crash, I tried
the 8056 Copy routine on their
Tech Tips Tape, but as it failed
to work I can only assume that
it was intended for use with the
Interface One. I am therefore
hoping desperately that you, or
one of your readers can help me.
Since Crash turned into a 'Games
Rag'I have felt vs though I have
no one to turn to on serious
computer problems or just for
seeking advice. Luckily for me,
the last useful information
Crash gave me was about OUTLET,
so I am secure again. I am not
usually one to write, but as I
have decided to subscribe to
OUTLET and send a disk every
month,I will take this opportun-
ity to state my views and send
in any software I have written.

I would also appreciate it if
you would put my full address in
OUTLET as I'm eager to communic-
ate with anyone with a spectrum
and any other hardware which I
have.
          Yours sincerely,

           Steven Watkins

P.S.  What is the best date to
send in my disk each month for
the next issue of OUTLET (By
subscription)?

P.P.S Do you know where I can
purchase a teletext adaptor,even
if it is not +2 or +D compatible
(I have an old 48K as well.)

To:Steven Watkins from Ron&Brian

If you are sending in your own
disk each month then please send
it in as soon as possible after
receiving your current issue of
OUTLET. We close our Order Book
on the 25th of each month to
ensure that the new issue of
OUTLET goes out during the first
week of the month of the cover
date. This takes a lot of hard,
concentrated effort and the
incoming mail has to be put to
one side until the job is done.
However, if your order is late
coming in, this does not mean
that you will "miss" your issue
of OUTLET - it just means a few
extra days wait whilst the
backlog of mail is dealt with.

Sigh! We need lots more info to
help with the printer problem!
Please send details of graphics
mode on you printer and details
of your printer interface. The
easiest way is to send a photo-
copy of the relevant page from
your printer manual and from
whichever interface you are
using. Are you using the +2
printer port (is there one?) or
the +D printer port (is there
one?).

Have you used OUR high-res dump?
If not, try, say,GLOBEPLOTTER or
COSINFANTUTI from last month. If
it doesn't work tell us EXACTLY
what you get, e.g.if the printer
prints garbage or nothing etc.
                  - Ron & Brian

From Leif Mortensen, DENMARK


Hi there,

Where can I get STATIC RAM 6264
(8K) or 62256 (32K)at reasonable
prices?






Sorry, Leif, I've been unable to
find a supplier. Can anyone else
help?
                        - Brian

From Richard McGee, WARRINGTON


Dear Ron & Brian,

My Spectrum is not playing the
game by the rules! For some
uncanny reason it works fine
until I attach my +D interface
then it buzzes,flashes interfer-
ence lines on the screen, NEWs
itself and adamantly refuses to
access the disc drive. The +D
works ok on a friend's Spectrum.

Can you help or should I take
the tape version of OUTLET now
and transfer it to disc when I
get a SAM COUPE?

To Richard McGee from Brian

Don't expect to be able to LOAD
ANY present version of OUTLET
into the new SAM COUPE without
modification or even re-writing!

I think you will have to bite
the bullet and send your Plus D
and Spectrum for repair. Try VSE
(see OUTBOARD).I have heard some
Spectrums can have a fault which
causes no trouble until say, an
Interface 1 is attached.

Alternatively, why not ring MGT
for advice or buy a cheap second
hand Spectrum? You might see one
going for say, `30 to `40. The
repair to your present one may
cost `20 or more.
                   - Brian

From: Jim Hargrave, ASHFORD

I am using VU-FILE which I have
transferred to microdrive using
an Interface 3. My problem is to
get the data files also onto
microdrive as it's very tedious
loading them from tape...


Try using BREAK while SAVEing or
LOADing a data file. If VU-FILE
is not protected and uses BASIC
to access tape then you should
see an error message. Note the
line number and alter the syntax
from tape to microdrive.

Is there any reader who has done
this conversion who might help?

                - Brian

From Terry Hayes, SURREY



I wonder if anyone can help me?

Some of you may remember and
have typed in this program. It
was a window-scrolling program
from the ZX Monthly, June, 1987
by Allen Davis. I have a copy of
this which I typed in at the
time but have been confronted
with the error-handling bug
"INVALID FILE NAME". Can anyone
help? I have tried everything.It
is a very well-written program
and I would like to us it.

                   - Terry

To Terry Hayes from Brian

I assume you mean you can't LOAD
the program but you don't say
which system you are using. The
error message doesn't mean there
is anything wrong with the pro-
gram but you are entering a file
name your system cannot accept,
e.g.longer than 10 characters or
no characters. CAT the disc and
check the filename carefully of
the BASIC program. If it also
LOADs in code, check the name of
that too. In that case you must
alter the line in the BASIC that
loads the code. I guess you are
using Opus as other systems give
different messages. Are you now
using some sort of menu loader
program?If so try a direct LOAD!
                      - Brian

          Mr M. Flanz,
       17 Northgate Close,
           Whittlesey,
      Peterborough,PE7 1RB.

Dear Ron & Brian,

I have a problem concerning my
PLUS D and large shaded dumps.
You see I own a Brother HR-5
printer and it does not under-
stand the ESC * function. I
wondered if you or any of your
readers knows of a routine to
enable me to do this. I would be
very greatful for any help.

          Many thanks,

            Mike Flanz

To Mike Flanz from Brian

I'm almost certain the HR5 DOES
use the ESC * printer code to
switch to graphics mode because
we have readers using our own
high-res dump. Try GLOBEPLOTTER
in last month's issue which does
a normal-size dump using ESC *

You do not say what results you
DO get. Are you getting too many
line feeds or garbled text or no
line feeds or nothing at all?

The only oddity I know about the
HR5 in this connection is one of
the line feed codes gives double
the size of standard Epson. Can
you give more details of results
and a copy of the relevant page
from your +D instructions?-Brian.

From David Wornham, WORCS.

Dear Brian and Ron,

To overcome sending letters in
32 column, how about producing
the magazine in 64 column,
changeable on screen to 32 for
reading, as done by the SDC?

How about making OUTLET fully
128K compatible if possible.Your
current CONTENTS page requires
SCROLL? which makes a flashing
letter one place too low.

Thanks for TAS-EXTRA.One problem
is "word forward"(INV.VIDEO)only
works for the 1st 1 or 2 words.

How about some clip art?

To David Wornham from Brian

Our entire text routines would
need to be re-written to give 64
column text and I, personally,do
not find it comfortable to read
on a Spectrum TV display. I'd
prefer say, 50 columns. However,
you say you would like 64 col.
"to overcome sending letters in
32 column". YOU DO NOT NEED TO
SEND LETTERS IN 32 COLUMN! (See
Page 02). It is far easier for
me if readers send in Tasword 2
files set at 32 column but not
essential. However,in your case,
I never received the text file!
Your letter is printed out in 32
column but since I have to type
the whole lot in again it does
not matter if it's written in

diagonal pink-striped chocolate
through the middle of a stick of
Blackpool rock! (Groan!- NOW I'm
asking for it!) All that matters
is I get the text file! You see,
I would MUCH prefer a Tasword 3
file in 64 columns,I can convert
to Tasword 2 and reformat to 32
columns than a print-out which I
have to type back in the machine
from whence it originally came!!

While I'm at it, can I whinge at
those who send letters printed
out from a wordprocessor with a
blank disc!It's no effort to put
the text file on the disc if you
are sending it anyway. Think of
my poor fingers! You know you'd
rather I spend my time writing a
crackin' program for you, right?

Sorry about that. Where were we,
David? Oh yes, now we have a +3
you should find OUTLET more 128K
compatible - obviously the +3
version is but I'm not sure, for
example,how a +2 m/drive version
will react in 128K mode to
FAILSAFE which is used to detect
if one or two drives are in use.
Perhaps someone can let us know?

I have TAS-EXTRAS running as I
type this and the "word forward"
works fine. Remember, you must
switch OFF the TAB function or
how can both work together? If
you have a TAB set at column 32
then INV. VIDEO goes to it and
ignores any words in between.The
TAB function REPLACES the "word
forward" command but you can
switch between them as desired.

I'd love to do some CLIP ART in
OUTLET but I'm still waiting for
someone to explain the format to
me. Will an ordinary SCREEN$ do?
Any suggestions about subject
matter?

Back on the subject of 128K mode
compatibility, can readers avoid
using the printer buffer for
code and not use the last two
UDGs - "T" and "U". Thanks.

               - Brian

From John White, LEICESTER


Dear Ron and Brian,

I notice that two readers were
puzzled as to how to obtain a
screen dump of Omnicalc 2 Histo-
grams. I also am interested to
know how it is done.

I, also,found CHARMASTER crashes
in Mode 6.I have the SDC version
too and this does not crash! I
wonder if editing etc. had
anything to do with it...

If only there were something on
the same lines to design char-
acters for my 120-D printer!

To John White from Brian

Sorry, yes it must be my editing
of CHARMASTER. I had to make
extensive changes to include
tape options, different printer
options and I seem to remember
having to hack the code to get
it to return to BASIC normally.

If your 120D printer accepts
down-loaded fonts then send me a
copy of the details from your
manual and I'll see if I can do
a simple routine for you or
modify one of our earlier char-
acter generators. If it doesn't
accept new fonts then you need a
program like WORDMASTER which I
assume uses graphics mode to
print different text styles.
                     - Brian

From I.A.G. Ross, RENFREWSHIRE


Dear Mr. Cavers,

   Regarding T3TO2, Tasword 3 IS
available for the Disciple/+D. I
have them both but cannot get
T3TO2 to work with them,probably
because the text files are in
machine code- 48K files starting
at 47847 and 128K at 49152.


A few queries...

1) Tas-sign, Qualitas and PCB
Typeliner permit a few control
codes only - any way of rigging
them so they will pemit the use
of Star LC-10 colour codes?

2) The LC-10 manual has a useful
looking program to download
characters but not in Spectrum
BASIC. Can anyone translate it,
put it on disc and sell it me?

3) Has anyone discovered how to
use Tasprint on +D or Disciple
disc?

4) Can the latest Masterfile for
Spectrum +3 be adapted for use
with a Spectrum 128K with Plus D
disc?
                 - I.A.G. Ross

Please send in your next letter
as a Tasword 3 Disciple file and
I'll see what is needed to alter
it to Tasword 2. Can anyone help
with the other queries?
                       - Brian.


Если больше — программа намертво зависает. Это можно частично обойти, добавив в BASIC-программу следующую строку:

```text
350 IF PEEK 34818 > 40 THEN POKE 34818,40
```

Эта строка предотвращает декодирование, просмотр или печать страниц сверх 40. Это лучше, чем ничего, и вскоре я пришлю доработку для печати текста целиком.

Небольшое замечание: вместо клавиш «F» и «B» для перехода на следующую и предыдущую страницы я использую клавиши со стрелками, поскольку на клавиатуре «+» они расположены в нижнем ряду. Изменение вносится в строку 520 Бейсика OUTPRINT путем подстановки CHR$ 9 и CHR$ 8 вместо "F" и "B". (Brian, почему бы не сделать "F" OR CHR$ 9...?) Следующая микропрограммка должна помочь вам разобраться с проблемами принтера касательно DAG. После инициализации интерфейса (ТОКЕНЫ ДОЛЖНЫ БЫТЬ ОТКЛЮЧЕНЫ!!):

```text
 5 INPUT "DAG CODE? (76,89 OR 90. )"; C ; "BYTES (<256)";I;" & J (keep small)";J
 10 LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ C;CHR$ I;CHR$ J;
 20 INPUT "X (<256) ";X:FOR N=1 TO I+256*J:LPRINT CHR$ X;:NEXT N
```

Отправка «27», а затем C на принтер должна перевести его в режим DAG (одинарная, двойная или учетверенная плотность в зависимости от того, равен ли C 76, 89 или 90); I + 256 * J указывает количество байтов, которые будут отправлены в этом режиме, и принтер не выйдет из него, пока это количество не будет получено.

Значение X определяет, какие иголки принтера сработают. Если X=1, сработает только нижняя игла, если 2 — следующая над ней, 4 — еще выше, а 7 — три нижних (Что! Забыли двоичную систему? — См. статью о числах в OUTLET №6). Если вы введете I=8 и X=1, то 8 байт напечатаются в виде подчеркивания. При X=255 будет напечатан сплошной блок длиной в один символ...

Если нет — вы не вошли в режим DAG, поэтому сверьте КОДЫ с вашей инструкцией. В OUTPRINT эти коды отправляются перед каждой операцией печати. Они находятся в строке кодов, начинающейся с адреса 64953, и включают в себя...

```text
27,78,9,27,51,24,27,c,144,3
```

Первые три задают пропуск в 9 строк; следующие три устанавливают межстрочный интервал 24/216" (что дает непрерывную графику); а последние предназначены для режима DAG с 144 + 256 * 3 = 912 байт, что рассчитано на 3-колоночную строку с пробелами...

Если ваша система нормально входит в режим DAG, но проблемы остаются, проверьте коды SKIP и межстрочного интервала.

Если трудности не исчезнут, пишите мне не раздумывая. Все, что удастся решить, будет передано в OUTLET. Обсуждать все через эти страницы может быть слишком долго (задержка минимум на месяц, а то и на два). Мой адрес и прочее — в начале этого письма.
